correctness.rationale: PASS. Gaussian translation integrals give c0(b)>0, c1(b)=∫(t-b)e^{-(t-b)^2/4}dν/√2, c2(b)=∫(t-b)^2e^{-(t-b)^2/4}dν/(2√2)≥0. Dominated convergence for finite positive ν yields smoothness and coefficient decay as |b|→∞ so maximal projected energies exist. Derivative identities c0'=c1/√2 and c1'=c2-c0/√2 imply Q0'=√2 c0 c1, Q1'=2c1 c2. Any maximizer of Q1 has c1=0: if c2=0 positivity forces single delta at b and therefore c1=0. Thus max Q1<=max Q0 while Q1>=Q0 pointwise, and both argmax sets coincide via Q0 stationarity. For non-atomic/non-singleton ν, c2>0 at optimal b makes Q2 strictly larger. Symmetric doublet stationary b=a tanh(ab/2) yields unique 0 center up to a²<=2, then ± nonzero centers; signed φ1 violates positivity hypothesis. Independent quadrature/derivative and center checks match these equations; arbitrary-measure assertions rely on analytic positivity/compactness, not discrete tests.
